title: AI helped build this one-bumper physics puzzle. Every score is checked by replaying the shot.
author: soulbeddu
selftext:
Nudge is a free game I’m launching inside Reddit. Move one orange bumper, drop the blue ball, and try to land it in the green pocket. The clip replays a practice course using the actual game physics.

**[Play Nudge here](https://www.reddit.com/r/NudgeDaily/comments/1ws2iud/)**

I’m the creator/publisher; Codex generated and revised the implementation. The stack is React, TypeScript, and Devvit Web. There is no generative AI running during gameplay.

The part that needed careful verification was whether the puzzles were actually solvable. The build includes a solver and tests for three-star solutions across all 84 daily courses. The same fixed-step simulation runs in the browser and on the server: the client sends the bumper position, and the server replays the shot to calculate the score. Player-made courses also need a verified successful shot before publishing.

There are 22 automated tests now, plus browser viewport and deployed-game checks. Independent phone feedback is still needed. One early layout mistake put the share button too far below the board; the current version puts the score and share action directly under it.

For anyone building physics games with AI assistance, what bugs have slipped past your automated tests? I’d also welcome feedback on whether this bounce feels satisfying to play.
